Times |date=12 October 2021}} Munitions India primarily manufactures [[ammunition]], [[explosives]], [[rocket (weapon)|rockets]] and [[bomb]]s for the use of the [[Indian Armed Forces]], foreign militaries and domestic civilian use. The budget allocated for MIL has seen an increase in the 2020s. The defence [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|PSU]] was allocated a budget of Rs 577 crore in FY2023, Rs 580 crore in FY2024 (RE), and Rs 745.45 crore in FY2025, the highest among the seven defence PSUs. This is a part of the infrastructure modernisation plan, and to increase the war reserves of the Indian Armed Forces to sustain long-drawn wars. The sum is to be invested in modernising equipment, increasing production capacity, and including new manufacturing lines for ammunition of 30mm and 40mm [[Grenade launcher|grenade launchers]]. Shell ==== As of February 2020, [[IIT Madras]], in partnership with [[IIT Kanpur]], [[Armament Research and Development Establishment]] and [[Research Centre Imarat]], is working on redesigning an existing [[155 mm caliber|155 mm shell]] using [[ramjet]] propulsion that can cover 60 km+ range. It will be made compatible with [[Haubits FH77]], [[Dhanush (howitzer)|Dhanush]], [[K9 Thunder#India|K9 Vajra-T]] and [[ATAGS (howitzer)|ATAGS]]. The shell will incorporate a Precision Guidance Kit for trajectory correction. IIT Madras will ensure that Munitions India can manufacture the shells. A number of technological advances have already been verified. The development team is awaiting product validation and prototyping now that the design is complete. Prototype is expected to be developed within three to four years.{{cite news |last1=MP |first1=Sidharth |date=21 February 2020 |title=IIT-M working on next-gen Ramjet-powered 155mm artillery shells for Indian Army |url=https://www.wionews.com/india-news/iit-m-working-on-next-gen-ramjet-powered-155mm-artillery-shells-for-indian-army-282090 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921163017/https://www.wionews.com/india-news/iit-m-working-on-next-gen-ramjet-powered-155mm-artillery-shells-for-indian-army-282090 |archive-date=21 September 2020 |access-date=22 August 2022 |publisher=WION}} The project was started in 2020 by partnering with the [[Army Technology Board]]. Early trials of a scaled down system was conducted from an IIT Madras developed 76 mm gun confirmed the fundamental idea. Internal and external ballistics were validated by subsequent testing carried out in September 2025 at the [[Regiment of Artillery (India)#School and Centre|School of Artillery]], which successfully demonstrated clean gun exit, stable flight, and ramjet activation.{{Cite news |date=2026-01-12 |title=IIT Madras develops ramjet-assisted Artillery Shells |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2213738®=3&lang=1 |access-date=2026-01-13 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}{{Cite news |last=Singh |first=Surendra |date=2026-01-09 |title=In a 1st in world, Army set to deploy ramjet-powered shells for 155mm artillery guns |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/in-a-1st-in-world-army-set-to-deploy-ramjet-powered-shells-for-155mm-artillery-guns/articleshow/126330397.cms |access-date=2026-01-12 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} With this approach, the range of conventional shells will be enhanced by 30–50% without losing their lethality. It was approved by the Army Technology Board. It can be retrofitted onto all the existing 155 mm artillery shells. As of December 2025, developmental tests at [[Pokhran#Pokhran Test Range|Pokhran Field Firing Range]] and IIT Madras had been successful, showing that the shell can depart the gun efficiently at wider operational zones.{{Cite web |last=Baruah |first=Sanjib Kr |date=2025-12-31 |title=Indian Army to be world’s first to use ramjet-powered 155 mm artillery shells |url=https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2025/12/31/indian-army-to-be-worlds-first-to-use-ramjet-powered-155-mm-artillery-shells.html |access-date=2026-01-01 |website=The Week |language=en}} By 12 January 2026, IIT Madras successfully conducted successful in-house tests of the ramjet unit. The ramjet engine was incorporated into an in-service 155 mm artillery shell, replacing the traditional [[base bleed]] unit. The project is led by IIT Madras [[Aerospace Engineering]] department faculty P.A. Ramakrishna and retired Indian Army officer [[Lieutenant general (India)|Lt General]] P R Shankar among others. Range improvements were demonstrated in trials carried out on different artillery platforms. The range in [[K9 Thunder#India|K9 Vajra-T]] increased from 36 km to approximately 62 km, in [[Dhanush (howitzer)|Dhanush]], the range is from approximately 30 km to approximately 55 km, and in [[ATAGS (howitzer)|ATAGS]], it is from approximately 40 km to nearly 70 km.{{Cite news |last=Sarkar |first=Shankhyaneel |date=2026-01-12 |title=IIT Madras Tests Ramjet-Assisted Artillery Shells That Extend Gun Range By Nearly 50% |url=https://www.news18.com/india/iit-madras-tests-ramjet-assisted-artillery-shells-extends-gun-range-by-nearly-50-ws-kl-9826178.html |access-date=2026-01-13 |work=news18.com}} A [[Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher#Ramjet propulsion|similar technology]] is expected to be developed for [[rocket artillery]]. ==== 155 mm Smart Artillery Shell ==== The development of 155 mm Smart Ammunition for the [[Regiment of Artillery (India)|Regiment of Artillery]] by Munitions India and [[IIT Madras]] was reported in February 2024. The period of development is roughly two years. The goal is to improve the accuracy and lethality of artillery shells during terminal impact. The smart shell can be launched from [[155 mm caliber|155 mm]] 39- and 45-[[Caliber (artillery)|calibre]] guns including [[Dhanush (howitzer)|Dhanush]], [[ATAGS (howitzer)|ATAGS]] and K9 Vajra-T. It will achieve a [[circular error probable]] (CEP) of {{Convert|10|m||abbr=on}} against {{Convert|500|m||abbr=on}} CEP for conventional shells. It requires housing of miniaturize electronics and sensors package with guidance, navigation, and [[Control surface (aviation)|control system]]. To improve accuracy, the smart artillery round will use [[NavIC]], with a [[GPS]] backup. It will be interoperable with all of the [[Indian Army]]'s artillery guns to accommodate various tactical requirements. The smart shell will incorporate three-mode fuse operation, fin stabilization, and [[Canard (aeronautics)|canard]] control.{{Cite news |date=2024-02-06 |title=IIT Madras to spearhead development of India's first Indigenous 155mm Smart Ammunition |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/iit-madras-to-spearhead-development-of-indias-first-indigenous-155mm-smart-ammunition/articleshow/107462407.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} A minimum range of {{convert|8|km|mi|abbr=on}} and a maximum range of {{convert|38|km|mi|abbr=on}} are anticipated. The smart shell will have three explosion modes: delayed, height of burst, and point detonation.{{Cite web |title=IIT Madras to develop smart ammunition {{!}} Indian Institute of Technology Madras |url=https://www.iitm.ac.in/happenings/press-releases-and-coverages/iit-madras-develop-smart-ammunition |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241127110656/https://www.iitm.ac.in/happenings/press-releases-and-coverages/iit-madras-develop-smart-ammunition |archive-date=2024-11-27 |access-date=2024-11-23 |website=www.iitm.ac.in}}{{Cite web |last=MP |first=Sidharth |date=5 February 2024 |title=IIT-M and Munitions India to develop smart ammo for 155mm artillery guns |url=https://www.wionews.com/india-news/iit-m-and-munitions-india-to-develop-smart-ammo-for-155mm-artillery-guns-687132 |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=WION |language=en-us}}{{Cite web |last=Bisht |first=Inder Singh |date=2024-02-09 |title=India Announces Maiden Precision Artillery Round Development |url=https://thedefensepost.com/2024/02/09/india-precision-artillery-round/ |access-date=2024-11-23 |website=The Defense Post |language=en-US}}{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2024-02-05 |title=IIT Madras to develop smart ammunition |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/iit-madras-to-develop-smart-ammunition/article67813804.ece |access-date=2024-03-20 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} == Exports == The UAE purchased 40,000 and 50,000 155 mm artillery ammunition in 2017 and 2019, respectively. In 2017 and 2019, the order was valued at approximately $40 million and $46 million, respectively. The known buyers of 155 mm shells have been the [[United Arab Emirates]] and [[Armenia]]. Unidentified European nation—likely [[Poland]] or [[Slovenia]]—just bought the artillery munitions, as per reports in February 2024.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-02-08 |title=Munitions India Bags Largest Export Order From Saudi Arabia; To Supply 155MM Artillery Shells Worth $225M |url=https://www.eurasiantimes.com/munitions-india-bags-largest-export-order-from-saudi-arabia-to-supply-155mm-artillery-shells-worth-225m/ |access-date=2024-02-08 |website=The EurAsian Times |language=en-US}}{{Cite news |last=Pubby |first=Manu |date=2019-08-03 |title=In its largest ever export order, OFB to supply 50,000 Bofors shells to UAE |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/in-its-largest-ever-export-order-ofb-to-supply-50000-bofors-shells-to-uae/articleshow/70501461.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} Videos from Ukraine have recently surfaced, showing the artillery ammunition manufactured in India being used by [[Ukrainian forces]] in [[Russo-Ukrainian War]]. Social media posts in both the Russian and Ukrainian languages reported what seemed to be Indian 155mm artillery shells likely falling into Ukraine. It was rumored that the weaponry consisted of MIL-produced HE ERFB BT shells.{{Cite news |last=Chaudhury |first=Dipanjan Roy |date=2024-01-05 |title=Russia flags supply of India-made 155mm artillery shells to Ukraine |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/russia-flags-supply-of-india-made-155mm-artillery-shells-to-ukraine/articleshow/106553525.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-02-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} MIL and its partner, Nadrah Company, inked a $225 million deal at World Defense Show 2024 to provide artillery ammunition to [[Saudi Arabia]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-02-07 |title=MIL inks $225-million ammunition contract with Saudi Arabia government |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/mil-inks-225-million-ammunition-supply-contract-to-saudi-arabia/article67821711.ece |access-date=2024-02-08 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} As of March 2024, Munitions India has export orders worth ₹6,000 crore, to be supplied till 2026-27. The leading customers are UAE, Vietnam, and one undisclosed country from Europe.{{Cite web |last=Ramesh |first=M. |date=2024-03-05 |title=Ammunitions maker Munitions India's export orders swell to ₹6,000 crore |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/ammunitions-maker-munitions-indias-export-orders-swell-to-6000-crore/article67916528.ece |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} In 2023 and early 2024, the company exported 500 tonnes of explosive to Germany's [[Rheinmetall]].{{Cite web |last=Philip |first=Snehesh Alex |date=2025-06-25 |title=Reliance Defence bags Rs 600 crore export order from Germany’s Rheinmetall |url=https://theprint.in/defence/reliance-defence-bags-rs-600-crore-export-order-from-germanys-rheinmetall/2670062/ |access-date=2025-06-26 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}} An initial shipment of 144 tonnes of explosive was done in October 2023. Two additional shipments were undertaken with the final shipment in March 2024.{{Cite news |last=Pubby |first=Manu |date=2024-10-05 |title=Alarm after defence PSU sells explosives to banned German Company |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/alarm-after-defence-psu-sells-explosives-to-banned-german-company/articleshow/113971338.cms |access-date=2025-06-26 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In FY 2023-24, about Rs. 2,000 crores (i.e. 28.5%) of contracts of MIL contracts were from export orders. The total business for the same period was of Rs. 7,000 crore by value.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Dalip |date=2024-07-25 |title=Govt’s capital infusion into MIL a sign for scaling-up explosive manufacturing capabilities to meet long-drawn war challenges |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/national/govts-capital-infusion-into-mil-a-sign-for-scaling-up-explosive-manufacturing-capabilities-to-meet-long-drawn-war-challenges/article68446004.ece |access-date=2024-07-26 |website=The Hindu Businessline |language=en}} ==See also== *Other PSUs formed from the Ordnance Factory Board:- **[[Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited]] (AWE), Kanpur **[[Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited]] (AVANI), Chennai **[[Gliders India Limited]] (GIL), Kanpur **[[India Optel Limited]] (IOL), Dehradun **[[Troop Comforts Limited]] (TCL), Kanpur **[[Yantra India Limited]] (YIL), Nagpur ==References== {{reflist}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India| state = collapsed}} [[Category:Defence companies of India]] [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 2021]]

Munitions India Limited (MIL) is an Indian state-owned defence company, headquartered in Pune, India, established in 2021 as part of the restructuring and corporatisation of the Ordnance Factory Board into seven different Public Sector Undertakings. Munitions India primarily manufactures ammunition, explosives, rockets and bombs for the use of the Indian Armed Forces, foreign militaries and domestic civilian use.
The budget allocated for MIL has seen an increase in the 2020s. The defence PSU was allocated a budget of Rs 577 crore in FY2023, Rs 580 crore in FY2024 (RE), and Rs 745.45 crore in FY2025, the highest among the seven defence PSUs. This is a part of the infrastructure modernisation plan, and to increase the war reserves of the Indian Armed Forces to sustain long-drawn wars. The sum is to be invested in modernising equipment, increasing production capacity, and including new manufacturing lines for ammunition of 30mm and 40mm grenade launchers.
